metadata.title: Micron bets $2.75 billion on India as AI memory demand surges

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Memory-chip maker Micron Technology Inc. (MU, Financials) has begun exporting chips from a new production operation that is barely starting to ramp, benefiting from rising AI infrastructure demand.Micron's semiconductor assembly and test plant in Gujarat, India is the result of around $2.75 billion in combined investment from the business and its government partners.Commercial production commenced earlier this year and DRAM and NAND products are already being supplied to customers throughout the world. The scale is already mind-boggling.The current output capacity of the plant is more than the memory required for the whole laptop market in India, said Sanjay Mehrotra, the CEO. And Micron intends to go much further.The business anticipates the Sanand factory to ramp up output of assembly and testing next year as worldwide demand for memory and storage continues to rise.Timing is key since AI has created a never-before-seen demand for memory supplies. Micron is investing in sophisticated production and packaging in the U.S., but India provides another place for assembly and testing.This means a wider worldwide production footprint as demand for memory increases.For investors, the next two things to monitor are how fast Sanand can scale next year and whether Micron can add capacity without hurting the extremely excellent pricing and margins that are fueling its AI memory boom right now.
